decision: Extract the post-impl _extract_codex_streaming_payload into a new shared codex_stream module rather than duplicating it; completion_dispatch imports it back (alias) so there is one source of truth and no circular import (completion_dispatch already imports sufficiency_auditor).
rationale: User point #4: reuse the known-good parser, don't fork it. completion_dispatch↔sufficiency_auditor import direction forced a neutral shared home.

decision: plan lock generates the sufficiency findings itself (CLI helper _ensure_sufficiency_findings) only for gated goal_types and only when missing; non-gated plans never trigger a paid call. No auditor configured → actionable message, gate's own refusal still guards.
rationale: User point #2: make lock generate, not dead-end — while respecting cost discipline (no paid call when the gate is a no-op).

decision: coerce_first_json_value uses json.JSONDecoder().raw_decode to read the first complete JSON value and ignore trailing content — the precise fix for the 'Extra data' shape that discarded the live paid Codex response.
rationale: User point #4/#5: the wasted response was valid JSON + trailing prose; strict json.loads rejected it.

decision: This plan was itself born from the dogfood that failed — running the full orchestrate loop on DontPanic. It is the highest-leverage outcome of that exercise (per operator) and precedes returning to the five feature plans.
rationale: Operator directive 2026-06-08: fix the governance loop first; these are not incidental bugs.

decision: Post-impl Codex audit (paid) returned needs_changes with 3 real findings, all fixed-forward: (1) the F002 model_dump(mode=json) fix was never actually applied — the first Edit was dropped and not redone; the audit caught it (live miss) — now applied at all 3 plan-review feed sites; (2) coerce_first_json_value scanned for the first [/{ anywhere, which would accept leading prose like 'I could not\n[]' as empty findings — now only tolerates TRAILING content after a leading value; (3) _ensure_sufficiency_findings used a raw-text regex that missed quoted YAML goal_type — now reuses sufficiency_gate._read_frontmatter so the gate + generator can't drift. +4 tests through the real paths. Live re-validation: generate_sufficiency_findings fired a REAL Codex call and parsed 4 findings (the path that crashed before). 490 focused tests green.
rationale: The audit-all-changes practice caught a fix that silently never landed — exactly the 'tests pass, production unchanged' trap. Fixed-forward with real-path tests.

decision: Plan intentionally LEFT at status:draft despite its work being merged. The fix shipped in PR #31 (commit e97b8fb) and was independently paid-audited per D005 (needs_changes, fixed-forward), but the completion-gate artifacts (evidence/goal-governance/post_impl/completion_findings.json + audit envelope) were never committed at merge time. enforce_completion_gate (goal_type:incident is gated) by design refuses a hand-edited draft->completed flip without that evidence, and `dontpanic plan close` additionally requires status:active (this plan is draft) and would re-run a paid audit. Operator decision (2026-06-09): do NOT bare-flip (defeats the gate), do NOT spend a fresh paid audit just to reconstruct missing ceremony, and do NOT fabricate evidence. Record the procedural gap honestly and leave the ledger at draft. The work itself is DONE and live on main; only the formal gate-close is absent. CodeRabbit (PR #33, closed) independently flagged the bare-flip attempt.
rationale: Honest-ledger over convenience: a gated plan's 'completed' status must be backed by gate evidence or a sanctioned override; neither is cleanly available, so draft is the truthful state.

title: Operator-sanctioned override close (draft -> completed) on prior-audit evidence
decision: Plan CLOSED status:draft -> status:completed by explicit operator authorization (2026-06-14), WITHOUT a fresh `plan close` paid audit. Rationale: the fix is merged to main (PR #31, commit e97b8fb) and was already independently paid Codex-audited at merge time per D005 (needs_changes -> all 3 findings fixed-forward); D006 deliberately left it draft only because the completion-gate artifacts (completion_findings.json + audit envelope) were never committed, NOT because the work was unverified. Re-running `plan close` would dispatch a redundant second paid audit of already-merged, already-audited code — which D006 explicitly refused and the one-paid-call discipline forbids. features.json F001-F003 flipped passes:true with evidence_refs (commit e97b8fb + PR #31) and verified_by=[codex,operator] per the schema's flip-with-evidence rule.
rationale: The completion gate exists to ensure code is audited before close; here it already was (D005, paid). The only gap was uncommitted gate artifacts, which the operator override legitimately substitutes for, avoiding a redundant paid call.
